acceptance_contract.quality: candidate must satisfy every prompt-required answer field and must not be worse than its paired control
acceptance_contract.price: candidate short- and long-context price-equivalent scenarios must both be strictly lower when request-level context classification is unavailable
acceptance_contract.speed: secondary and may regress after quality and both price scenarios pass
acceptance_contract.failure_recovery: a candidate intended for production must not depend on a failed command and recovery retry
acceptance_contract.stop: one quality, price, identity, or required-entry failure stops expansion for that candidate

oracle_calibration.problem: the historical TypeScript and C++ answer contracts promoted useful but unasked facts to required, so compliant answers could be scored as quality failures

forward_only_versions.change: the TypeScript prompt explicitly requests the two handler identities and source/runtime boundary; getSessions and the sessionSelected null branch are supporting
the C++ prompt explicitly requests the qualified source/runtime boundary; compiler binding and numeric correctness remain supporting
a C# case freezes qualified identities, direct calls, branches, fallback semantics, completeness, and a source/runtime boundary

oracle_calibration.history_policy: v11 through v13 remain immutable after experiment identity binding; corrections only apply through a new corpus version

experiments.name: typescript-large-page-with-answer-check
experiments.decision: reject: lower price and elapsed cannot override one missing required branch

experiments.name: typescript-large-page-with-nonmerging-output-contract
experiments.decision: pass this case: complete required quality and both price scenarios strictly lower; command count is not a sampling count

experiments.name: cpp-same-rules-before-syntax-clarification
experiments.candidate_failure: srcq rg -- rg --files repeated the backend name and required a corrected command
experiments.decision: reject as a production entrance despite quality and price pass because candidate relied on failed-command recovery

experiments.name: cpp-same-rules-with-syntax-clarification
experiments.decision: pass this case: complete required quality, no failed command, and both price scenarios strictly lower; speed regression is allowed

experiments.name: csharp-cross-language-stop-case

quality.control_required: incomplete: SlotIndex ordering was not explicit; preliminary audit also found no unified completeness statement

experiments.decision: reject-and-stop: candidate quality is complete and no failed command occurs, but both price scenarios and elapsed increase

tool_decision.srcq_large_page_probe: srcq 0.7.0 returned the complete 473-line, 21157-character TypeScript multi-anchor page with no @more, @next, or @cut when limit 1000 and model token budget 12000 were explicit
tool_decision.owner_analysis: srcq deliberately preserves native argv. A leading rg after the explicit boundary can also be a legitimate ripgrep pattern, so silently stripping it would corrupt valid native semantics and contradict forwarding tests.
tool_decision.decision: do not modify srcq; the experiment-only syntax clarification removed the observed candidate failure without changing the tool contract

conclusions.claim: the explicit large-page query is a missing srcq product capability
conclusions.evidence: the direct srcq 0.7.0 probe returned the complete page without continuation markers

conclusions.claim: a generic non-merging output contract can preserve required answer completeness
conclusions.status: supported in the tested TypeScript, C++, and C# cases
conclusions.evidence: candidate required scores were 6/6, 7/7, and 8/8 after prompt-oracle calibration

conclusions.claim: the shared candidate core plus syntax clarification strictly lowers price across every expanded project
conclusions.evidence: the C# candidate raised short price from 40342.0 to 57144.8 and long price from 74072.0 to 107179.6

conclusions.claim: fewer raw commands are necessary for lower price
conclusions.evidence: the accepted TypeScript and C++ case-level candidates used one and two more commands respectively while both price scenarios decreased

conclusions.claim: command syntax recovery should be implemented by normalizing repeated backend tokens in srcq
conclusions.evidence: the repeated token is ambiguous with a valid native search pattern; normalization would break the native argv preservation contract

repository_decision.benchmark_corpus_change: retain v12-v14 and this audit as forward-only evidence
repository_decision.further_matrix_expansion: stopped on the first cross-language price counterexample

limitations: Each identity contains one control and one candidate run, so no repeat variance is estimated.
The runner exposes aggregate subject usage, not per-request usage or request context class.
Command counts are structural observations and are not exact sampling counts.
The evidence covers only the bound TypeScript, C++, and C# snapshots with gpt-5.6-luna medium/default.
The C# control had one recovered skill-path command failure; candidate price was still higher even though it had no failed command and better required coverage.
